name: Warp Calendar Events
author: Saurabh Guttedar

sections.description:
Warp Calendar Events helps you publish and organize events in WordPress. Manage events, venues, organizers, categories and tags from an interactive dashboard, then display published events on your website.

Get Warp Calendar Events Pro | Compare Free and Pro

  • Month, List, Day, Week, Week list, Week timeline and Upcoming views.
  • Classic, Minimal and Compact templates with light, dark and device-based appearance options.
  • Daily, weekly, monthly-date and yearly recurrence, interval/count/end-date limits and individual occurrence changes.
  • Twelve Gutenberg blocks, an event-layout pattern, shortcodes and an upcoming-events widget.
  • Dedicated Calendar, Upcoming Events and Event Details integrations for Elementor and Bricks, when installed separately.
  • Public iframe and script embeds for another website.
  • Manual CSV and public HTTPS ICS preview/import, preserving previously imported records and local edits.
  • ICS downloads, rolling subscriptions, Google Calendar compose links and event structured data.
  • Optional mapping of existing public post types and date fields into the calendar.
  • Registration: free RSVP or paid tickets per event, per-occurrence capacity, group bookings, guest self-service links, confirmation emails and private attendee lists with CSV export.
  • PayPal tickets using your own PayPal business account — no WooCommerce, no platform fee. Verified captures, webhooks, full and partial refunds and reconciliation.
  • Migration from The Events Calendar 6.x and Pie Calendar 1.x with inventory, dry run, batched import, rerun safety, optional URL redirects and rollback.
  • Ticket types per event (prices, per-date stock, sale windows, per-booking limits), discount codes and offline payments with staff-recorded receipts.
  • Guest self-service date changes within the same event at unchanged ticket quantities and base prices, with capacity checks, audit history and replacement access links.
  • Editable scheduled announcements and coupon rules, signed-in customer coupon limits and a payment-due booking filter.
  • Unicode PDF documents with bundled licensed fonts; shaped Indic and right-to-left text and a CJK fallback.
  • Optional WooCommerce checkout for paid bookings, using any payment method your store offers.
  • Up to three attendee questions per event, a My bookings page for logged-in guests, PDF confirmations, tickets, invoices and credit notes.
  • Branded, editable emails, automatic reminders, announcements to guests and a payment-received email.
  • Waitlists: guests join a full date, freed places are held for the next guest with an expiring offer, and paid places go to the normal checkout.
  • Speakers and performers, timed agendas (with date-specific agendas for repeating events) and public venue, organizer and speaker directories.
  • Online and hybrid events with a private meeting link shown only to the guests you choose, from the time you choose. The link never appears in public pages, feeds or calendar files.
  • Venue, organizer and format filters, and an events map with an accessible list (maps load only when a visitor asks).
  • Reports with gross, net, received, refunded and unpaid totals, CSV and PDF exports.
  • Optional newsletter sign-up through MailPoet, always an unticked, separate choice.
  • Optional AI access through the WordPress Abilities API (MCP Adapter compatible): read and write are separate opt-ins, guest personal data is withheld by default.
  • Event Tickets booking-history import for events already moved from The Events Calendar.

JavaScript and CSS source files are included locally; no build step or external CDN is required. Elementor and Bricks are optional and are not bundled. Core features, RSVP, PayPal tickets and migrations work without builders or the separate Warp Calendar Events Pro add-on. Events stay display-only until you enable registration.

Warp Calendar Events Pro

The separately installed Pro add-on adds Stripe Checkout, QR check-in, conditional attendee questions, managed Zoom and Google Meet meetings, Mailchimp, scheduled ICS imports, signed outbound webhooks, Photo view and advanced recurrence.

View Pro features and buy a license.

External services and privacy

The Free plugin sends no telemetry. Read the External Services and Privacy page for data storage, retention, export, deletion, waitlist recovery and PDF image handling.

Optional external connections are used as follows:

  • ICS preview/import requests the chosen HTTPS feed from your server, sharing the request and server IP with that provider. Its policies depend on the feed you choose.
  • Google Calendar receives public event details when a visitor opens Add to calendar. Google Maps receives the venue address when directions are opened, or the visitor’s IP and venue coordinates when Show map is selected. Google privacy, terms.
  • OpenStreetMap receives the visitor’s IP and venue coordinates when an OpenStreetMap preview is opened with Show map. Privacy, tile policy.
  • PayPal receives the booking reference, amount, currency and event description during configured paid checkout and related payment operations. Privacy, terms.

Optional WooCommerce and MailPoet integrations process orders and opted-in newsletter sign-ups on your site; configured gateways follow their own policies. Following online-event links contacts the chosen meeting provider. Embedded calendars request public data from the originating WordPress site.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the warp-calendar folder to wp-content/plugins, or install its ZIP using Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Warp Calendar Events.
  3. Open Warp Calendar Events > Events, choose Add Event, enter a title and schedule, then save as Published.
  4. Insert the Warp Calendar Events block into a page, or use [warp_calendar].
  5. Use Embed calendar in the dashboard for builder instructions and external embed snippets.
sections.faq:
How do registration and tickets work?

Edit an event, open Registration & tickets, enable registration, choose Free RSVP or Paid ticket (PayPal), and set places per occurrence. Each date of a repeating event has its own capacity. Visitors register on the event page without an account and receive an email with a private link to view or cancel. Manage bookings in Warp Calendar Events > Bookings. Add ticket types, discount codes, offline payment and a waitlist in the same section. QR codes and check-in are part of Pro.

What do I need for PayPal tickets?

A PayPal business account and a REST app (client ID and secret) from the PayPal Developer Dashboard, your merchant ID, and a webhook pointing to the URL shown in Warp Calendar Events > Payments. Test with sandbox credentials first. Payments go directly to your PayPal account. Warp adds no fee; PayPal charges its own processing fees under your agreement with PayPal. Supported currencies are those PayPal supports for REST checkout (for example USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, CAD, JPY). Your site needs a public HTTPS address for webhooks.

How are refunds and cancellations handled?

Guests can cancel free bookings themselves before the cutoff you set; for paid bookings they can request cancellation. Refunds are a separate administrator action in Bookings: you choose the amount and how many places to release, and the booking changes only after PayPal confirms the refund. Editing or deleting an event never refunds anyone automatically, and events with active bookings cannot be deleted until they are resolved.

What does the migrator copy?

From The Events Calendar 6.x: events (title, content, excerpt, status, password, featured image, dates, time zone, all-day and multi-day meaning), venues, the first organizer, categories, tags, website, display cost and cancelled/postponed status, as new Warp events. From Pie Calendar 1.x: your existing posts, pages and custom post types are enabled in place, so their content and URLs stay the same. Not migrated: ticket, RSVP, order and attendee history, payment credentials, licences, CRM settings and Events Calendar Pro recurring series (these are listed in the dry-run report). Source plugins and their data are never changed or deleted.

Can I undo a migration?

Yes. Rollback removes records the migration created and restores values it changed, but keeps anything you edited afterwards (flagged for review), shared media and terms, and stops entirely if bookings exist for migrated events. URL redirects are a separate on/off switch.

Should I run a real cron job?

Confirmation emails, payment reconciliation and hold expiry run through a retrying queue. WP-Cron only runs when your site gets visits. For reliable timing, disable WP-Cron and run wp warp-calendar tasks every minute from your server’s cron.

Can I roll back to an earlier version?

Back up your database before updating. Versions 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 add database tables; installing an older ZIP again does not remove them or undo bookings, and older code ignores features it does not know (waitlists, ticket types, offline payments). Before downgrading, close registration and resolve or refund open bookings. To fully revert, restore your database backup.

How do online events stay private?

Set the event format to Online or Hybrid, add the meeting link and choose who may see it (anyone, logged-in visitors, confirmed guests or paid guests) and how long before the start it appears. The link is never written into the event page, the public events feed, calendar files or search data, so page caches cannot leak it. Allowed visitors get it on request, on their private booking page and in their emails once the reveal time has passed.

Can AI assistants use my calendar?

Yes, if you allow it. Under Settings > Integrations > AI access you can let assistants read events, availability, waitlists, bookings and reports through the WordPress Abilities API (WordPress 6.9+), for example with the MCP Adapter plugin. Changes (draft events, event edits, recording offline payments) need a second switch. Both are off by default. Assistants act as the signed-in user, so they can only do what that user already may; refunds and charges are never available, and every change is logged. Guest names and emails are withheld unless you also turn on sharing personal data. Warp sends nothing to any AI service itself; the AI client you connect decides where its requests go.

How do waitlists work?

Turn on the waitlist in Registration & tickets. When a date is full, visitors can join it. When places free up, the first waiting guests whose request fits get an email offer that holds the places for the hours you set. Paid offers go to the normal checkout; nobody is charged automatically. Staff can see, remove and re-offer entries under Waitlists.

Do I need Pro or a builder?

No. All features listed above work in this plugin. Pro is installed separately and requires this plugin.

Does Add to Google Calendar synchronize calendars?

No. It opens an event draft for the visitor to review and save in Google. ICS downloads open in compatible calendar applications. Subscriptions are public rolling feeds covering the next 89 days; application refresh schedules vary.

What can the importer import?

Manual ICS and CSV imports accept up to 1 MB and 250 entries. ICS recurrence, detached exceptions, duration properties and custom VTIMEZONE definitions are skipped with an explanation. Imports do not run in the background or overwrite previously imported records automatically.

What happens on deactivation or deletion?

Event posts, contact metadata and settings remain in the WordPress database. Deactivation and deletion do not erase them. Back up your database before updating or removing plugins. Remove event/contact records through WordPress when no longer needed.

Which date formats are supported?

Interactive calendars support Y y F M m n d j l D H G h g i s a A T e tokens and backslash escapes. T and e display the timezone identifier. Dates use the Gregorian calendar and Latin digits. PHP Intl supplies localized date names when available; otherwise an installed WordPress language or the site language is used.

Where do I customize the booking PDFs?

In WordPress admin, open Warp Calendar Events > Payments > PDF documents. You can also use PDF settings on the Bookings or Payments screen. Set your business details, header and footer accent colors, and optional Media Library logo and signature. The logo can also appear as a faint watermark.
sections.changelog:
0.5.0

  • New: event revision history with side-by-side comparison and guarded restore.
  • Improved: mobile calendar filters with a collapsible panel and clear action.
  • New: PDF branding with header and footer accents, a logo, an optional watermark and a signature image.
  • Improved: admin form accessibility, release preview navigation and plugin lifecycle handling.

0.4.0

  • New: Guests can move eligible bookings to another available date of the same event. Ticket types, quantities and base prices stay the same, and existing payment records are preserved.
  • New: Edit scheduled announcements before they send, change coupon rules for future bookings, limit coupon use per signed-in customer, and filter bookings by payment due.
  • Improved: The WordPress dashboard groups navigation by workflow and adds clearer record search, publication and category filters, and Trash actions. Event editing has updated controls and featured image selection.
  • Improved: The AI settings screen offers guided assistant setup with copyable configuration and credential controls.
  • Improved: Calendar and booking views load availability for multiple dates together. Booking PDFs use bundled Unicode fonts for broader language support.
  • Fixed: Waitlists stop offering past dates or sending stale offers. Rescheduling revokes old booking management links and entry codes. Late payments with an exhausted coupon go to staff review.
  • Pro: Scheduled ICS imports and signed outbound webhooks are available in Sync & webhooks. Imported descriptions display as text, webhook payloads expire after 30 days, and signing secrets are encrypted and can be rotated. See the bundled integration guide for setup and limits.

0.3.0

  • Changed: database tables, staff capabilities and admin request names now use the warp_calendar_ prefix (tables become wp_warp_calendar_*), so they can never clash with other plugins using warp_. The upgrade renames them in place; nothing is copied or deleted. Old “Add to calendar” and subscription links keep working.
  • New: ticket types with prices, per-date stock, sale windows and limits; discount codes; offline payments with staff-recorded receipts and reversals.
  • New: optional WooCommerce store checkout; provider-neutral payment handling (PayPal keeps working as before).
  • New: up to three attendee questions per event; My bookings page; PDF confirmations, tickets, invoices and credit notes.
  • New: branded editable emails, reminders, announcements and a payment-received email; ticket lines in booking emails.
  • New: waitlists with held, expiring offers made as soon as places free up; Waitlists screen for staff.
  • New: speakers and performers, agendas with date-specific overrides, public directories with paging.
  • New: online and hybrid events with protected meeting links and timed reveal.
  • New: venue, organizer and format filters; events map with an accessible list and an optional one-click overview map.
  • New: reports with consistent money definitions, per-ticket breakdown, CSV and PDF exports.
  • New: optional MailPoet newsletter sign-up (consent-based); Event Tickets booking-history import.
  • New: opt-in AI access through the WordPress Abilities API (read, and separately write) with an AI privacy switch; Settings > Integrations tab for maps, newsletter and AI.
  • Improved: event category, tag and all-events pages list upcoming events by their next date, with date, time and venue, in any theme.
  • Improved: one content width for event details, booking and agenda; neutral dark mode; the calendar follows the accent colour; clearer booking page with ticket codes as cards.
  • Improved: admin app sections for speakers, online access, waitlist and newsletter; accessible tab titles on admin screens.
  • Fix: the booking form’s hidden anti-spam field no longer causes sideways scrolling on right-to-left sites.
  • Database: adds tables for ticket stock, waitlists and newsletter sign-ups; existing events, bookings and URLs are kept.

0.2.0

  • New: free RSVP and paid PayPal tickets per event with per-occurrence capacity, holds, group bookings, guest management links, confirmation emails and cancellation.
  • New: Bookings screen with filters, attendee details, resend, cancel, move to another date, refunds, PayPal reconciliation and spreadsheet-safe CSV export.
  • New: native PayPal checkout (no WooCommerce) with verified captures and webhooks, sandbox/live separation, full and partial refunds.
  • New: migration from The Events Calendar 6.x and Pie Calendar 1.x with dry run, batching, rerun safety, conflict detection, URL redirects and rollback.
  • New: durable task queue and wp warp-calendar tasks / wp warp-calendar migrate commands; personal-data export/erasure for bookings.
  • Fix: the no-refresh admin now works on sites without pretty permalinks.
  • Database: adds 11 tables; existing events, settings and URLs are unchanged.

0.1.0

Initial release candidate: event administration, seven views, three templates, recurrence, blocks, optional builder integrations, embeds, imports and exports.

upgrade_notice.0.3.0: Adds ticket types, waitlists, offline and store payments, speakers, online events and reports. Back up your database first: the update renames the plugin's tables to wp_warp_calendar_* and keeps existing events and bookings. Going back to 0.2.0 afterwards needs that backup.

screenshots.caption: Month view with recurring events, category, tag, venue, organizer and format filters, date jump and calendar subscriptions.
Event page with dates and time zone, status, venue and organizer cards, speakers and the agenda.
Visitors choose a date and ticket types, see the total update, enter a discount code and add attendee details.
Week list with event filters, venues, descriptions and "Add to calendar" links.
Events map with an optional OpenStreetMap overview and an accessible list of upcoming dates per venue.
Responsive list view on a 390-pixel phone screen.
Manage events and drafts in the admin app, with search, filters, duplication and recurrence summaries.
Ticket types with their own prices, places per date, booking limits and sale windows.
Agenda builder with sessions, rooms and speakers, plus date-specific agendas for recurring events.
Bookings overview with upcoming places, payments awaiting, money collected and how full each date is. All guest and payment data shown is fictional.
Reports for any date range, with gross and net sales, discounts, refunds and CSV or PDF export.
Saved calendars for a category, venue or audience, each with its own shortcode and a live preview.
Guests can move a booking to another available date of the same event at the same price.
Choose a template, light, dark or automatic appearance, the event accent colour, images and excerpts.
